MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron sits at the "name → what follows" boundary: it activates mildly on the verb or colon that comes right after a person's/product's name introducing descriptive content ("Peter Cousins **covers**", "Dan **provides**", "Lynn Taylor, **author** of", "Dry Shampoo**:**"), and is strongly *suppressed* by the visually identical colon when it follows a speaker name in interview/dialogue transcripts ("William**:** Yes…", "A**:** I chose…").

Fires on the head noun of the opening subject phrase in the first few tokens of a document (e.g. "trial", "students", "Minister", "court"), i.e. an early-sequence common-noun position, while being suppressed by mojibake/unicode junk, bullet markers, and slashes in that same opening position.
